title: Copilot Studio: discover and use shared plugins from Microsoft's plugin registry
summary: The roadmap facts, documented administration paths, commands and licensing background are supported. The changed billing page still supports the qualified Copilot Credits statement; no registry-specific default, switch or additional charge was found. Narrow the discoverability statement to the Copilot channel and the availability restrictions Microsoft describes.

claims.claim: The connector-block path is Power Platform admin center > Security > Data and privacy > Data policy > policy > Edit Policy > Next > Next > Assign connectors > connector > three dots > Block.
claims.quote: select **Security**, and then select **Data and privacy**; Select **Data policy**; select the data policy and select **Edit Policy**; Select **Next**; Select **Next**. The **Assign connectors** page appears; Select the three dots; select **Block**.

claims.claim: Add-ConnectorsToPolicy -PolicyName <policy GUID> -Connectors <connector objects> -Classification Blocked assigns the selected policy connectors to Blocked.
claims.quote:
Add-ConnectorsToPolicy
    [-PolicyName] <String>
    [-Classification] <String>
    [-Connectors] <Object[]>
Allowed values are 'General', 'Confidential', and 'Blocked' (for Non-business, Business, and Blocked, respectively).

claims.claim: The Add-ConnectorsToPolicy target parameter accepts a policy GUID.
claims.quote:
### -PolicyName
The policy name (GUID).

claims.claim: Each connector object for Add-ConnectorsToPolicy needs id, type and name.
claims.quote:
Each entry in the list is required to have 3 properties:
- id: The unique identifier of the connector.
- type: The type of the connector:
- name: The friendly name of the connector

claims.claim: Add-ConnectorsToPolicy moves an already classified connector from its previous group to the specified group.
claims.quote: If any of the connectors are already classified in a different group, they are moved to the specified group.
